get.summary: Get a content item

patch.description: `title`/`brief` change freely. Changing `caption` or `targetPlatforms` on approved, scheduled or failed content revokes the approval (back to draft, pending schedules cancelled); it is refused (409) while publishing or published.

delete.summary: Move a content item to the trash (or remove a trashed one for good)
delete.description: Moves the post to the trash (`deletedAt`; restore with `POST /api/contents/{id}/restore`) and stops its queued or running work (generation, render, checks, canvas jobs). It is purged with its generated files TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS later. Refused (409) while scheduled, publishing or published, and while a cancelled schedule's order is still at the cloud publisher (the worker cancels it there within seconds; an immediate sync is requested). `?permanent=true` removes a post that is already in the trash now. Deleting a trashed post again is a no-op.

post.summary: Take a content item back out of the trash
post.description: Clears `deletedAt`; the post is back on the board as it was (work stopped by the delete is not restarted). Restoring a post that is not in the trash is a no-op.

post.summary: Approve the current version by its hash
post.description: The body carries the hash of the version the user looked at. It must equal the current version's hash, otherwise 409 `hash_mismatch` (someone added a newer version). Allowed from draft or in_review; repeating it on approved content with the same hash is a no-op. The generation checks gate it: while the latest check run of that version has blocking results under the brand's check settings, or no run of it has finished yet (and the brand has checks on), it is refused with 409 `conflict` (a Turkish message about the checks; `issues` lists the blocking results) unless the body says `acknowledgeChecks: true`.

post.summary: Request a manual status change
post.description: Allowed: draft -> in_review, in_review -> draft, approved -> draft (revoke), failed -> draft, failed -> approved (only if the approval still matches). Approval itself uses /approve; scheduling uses /api/schedules.

get.summary: List versions (newest first, without slide HTML)

post.summary: Add a version (becomes current; content returns to draft)
post.description: The server computes the content hash. Any approval is cleared and pending schedules are cancelled, because approval is bound to a specific hash. Refused (409) while publishing or published.

get.summary: Get one version with its slides

patch.summary: Update version metadata (note, rendered assets, layer layouts)
patch.description: Slides are immutable; no field changes the content hash. On the version the content's approval covers, rendered images are frozen too (they are what gets published): a missing render may be filled in (it is rendered from the approved slide), but one that is set cannot be replaced or removed (409 `invalid_transition`) — add a new version instead, which needs a new approval.

post.summary: Restore an older version as a new version
post.description: Adds a new `manual_edit` version that copies the slides of `version` exactly (so the hash equals that version's hash); its renders, layer layouts and editor document are reused. Like any new version it clears the approval and cancels pending schedules. Refused (409) while publishing or published.

post.summary: Duplicate a content item as a new draft
post.description: Copies type, brief, caption and platforms, and the current version (slides, renders, layer layouts and the editor document) as version 1 of the copy. Approval, schedules and older versions are not copied.

get.description: Defaults (`updatedAt: null`) until they were saved once.

get.summary: Check runs of a content item (newest first)

post.description: Written by the worker. The server sorts the results (problems first) and computes the summary and the blocking count from the strictness.

get.summary: Follow jobs live (WebSocket)
get.description: WebSocket upgrade. Optional `jobId` (one job) or `brandId` (one brand); neither = all jobs. The server sends `jobs.snapshot` first, then `job.updated` and `presence` frames (schema `JobStreamMessage` in @studio/contract). Clients may send `ping`; reconnect and use the new snapshot after a drop.

get.summary: List jobs (newest first)

post.summary: Create a job
post.description: Stores the job as `queued` and notifies the Hub, which dispatches it to the Mac worker now or as soon as one connects (priority desc, then FIFO).

get.summary: Get a job

post.summary: Cancel a job
post.description: A queued job is cancelled at once. A running job gets `cancelRequestedAt` and stays `running` until the worker confirms (or the cancel grace period passes); follow it on the stream. 409 `invalid_transition` when the job already finished.

200.description: The job after the cancel request.

post.summary: Apply one instruction to many posts
post.description: HTML posts get one `content.generate` job each from their current version with the instruction (like the chat's `revise_post`). Canvas posts (a Wecra document is the design) go to the chat agent: one new conversation of their brand asks it to apply the instruction with its canvas tools, so the hand edits stay. Posts that cannot take it come back in `skipped` with a Turkish reason; approved or scheduled ones need `confirmApprovalLoss`.

200.description: What was queued and what was left out.

post.summary: Queue a failed or cancelled job again
post.description: A new job with the same type, brand, content and payload (RETRYABLE_JOB_TYPES; 400 for other types, 409 unless the job failed or was cancelled, or when its post is in the trash). A plan item's generation goes through its plan (`POST /api/plans/{id}/generate` with the item), so the item follows the new job and the plan's rules apply.

get.summary: How long and how much N post generations will take
get.description: Measured from the last finished `content.generate` jobs (back-to-back throughput, else the median duration) and the spend records of those jobs; a dated default when there is no history. Claude runs on the subscription (0 USD).

post.summary: Purge what has been in the trash too long
post.description: Posts and files in the trash longer than TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS are removed for good with their stored files (bounded per call). The Hub also runs it hourly.

Pictures must be images of the brand.

post.description: A new draft of the same brand linked to the post (`source`) and its `content.generate` job: a story (1080×1920, the brand's design, the post's texts adapted, safe areas kept) or a Reels (motion graphics from the post's slides and texts, its pictures as scenes).

The account must belong to the content's brand, not be disabled, and its platform must be one of the content's target platforms. Moves the content to `scheduled`. A `failed` schedule of the same content and account is reused (retry): it goes back to `pending` with the new time and keeps its id, so its cloud order is replaced instead of duplicated.

post.description: `product_image` / `variant`: the picture fills the post's slot (`slotId`) in a new rendered version (`job` is the `content.render`; no slot = nothing placed, `job` null). `product_photo_upgrade`: the picture replaces the product's photo; the old photo goes to the trash for TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS. The pictures not chosen go to the trash too (unless something else uses them). 409 unless pending.

post.summary: Reject: do not use the pictures
post.description: The request's pictures go to the trash (restorable for TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS) unless something else uses them (a post version, a product, another pending request…). 409 unless pending.

The old request's pictures go to the trash unless something else uses them. 409 for decided requests or when the original request is unknown.

post.description: Pictures must be `image` assets of the brand; the post, product, conversation and message must belong to it. `supersedesId` marks that pending request `superseded`. `chatMessage` (with `conversationId`, without `messageId`) posts an assistant message with the text and the request's card into the conversation.

post.description: The answer arrives as presence `tools`. 409 when no worker is connected.

post.summary: Install (or update) a tool on the Mac from its official source
post.description: Queues a `tool.install` job (follow it on /api/jobs/stream; presence `tools` shows the progress). The download is verified (SHA-256 / npm integrity / Developer ID signature) before anything is unpacked. A tool the Mac already has (`location: system`) is never installed over (409), nor one that cannot be installed in the app (409). A second request while one runs returns the running job.

202.description: The install job (queued or already running).

post.summary: Remove Studio's own copy of a tool
post.description: Queues a `tool.uninstall` job. A copy the Mac already had (Homebrew, PATH) is never touched: 409 when Studio has no copy of its own.

get.summary: Follow a conversation live (WebSocket)
get.description: WebSocket upgrade. Without `after` the server sends `conversation.snapshot`; with `after` (the last seq the client applied) it replays the stored events after it, then `conversation.resumed` (or a snapshot when `after` is too far behind). Live events follow, each with a gap-free `seq`. Schema: `ConversationStreamMessage` in @studio/contract. Clients may send `ping`.

get.summary: List conversations (most recently active first)

post.summary: Start a conversation (brand optional)

get.summary: Get a conversation

patch.summary: Rename, archive / unarchive, or set the brand once
patch.description: `brandId` is accepted only while the conversation has no brand (409 otherwise). An archived conversation accepts no new messages until it is unarchived.

get.summary: List messages (newest first; page backwards with cursor)

post.summary: Send a user message (starts an agent run)
post.description: Stores the message, creates an agent run and a `chat.turn` job (dispatched to the Mac worker now or when it connects). 409 `conflict` while another run of the conversation is queued or running, or when the conversation is archived. Attachments must be existing assets of the conversation's brand. Each attachment gets a conversation alias (`image`, `image-1`, ...; or the one requested in `attachments[].alias`, 409 if taken) and `@alias` tokens in the text are resolved into `message.mentions`. With a repeated `clientMessageId` the original message and run come back (200, `replayed: true`).

post.summary: Answer a question part of an assistant message
post.description: Records the answer on the question part (final; repeating the same answer is a no-op, a different one is 409). When no run is active, the answer starts a new agent run.

post.summary: Allow once / deny a consent card of the running agent
post.description: The agent waits on a `consent` part before an action that needs the owner's go (schedule, approve). `allow: true` lets it go ahead once; `false` denies it. Final: repeating the same decision is a no-op, a different one is 409, and an `expired` card (not answered in time, or its run ended) is 409. Unlike a question, a decision never starts a new run.

get.summary: List attachment aliases (oldest first, not paginated)
get.description: Every alias of the conversation with its asset metadata, a path that streams the file (`contentPath`), earlier names (`previousAliases`) and the message that introduced it.

patch.description: The alias keeps its id; its old name stays reserved for it (it still resolves in new text and is never given to another attachment). 409 `conflict` when the name is or was used by another alias of the conversation. Stored messages keep their text: clients show the current name by looking up `aliasId` of mentions and attachment parts.

get.summary: List agent runs of a conversation (newest first)
Get an agent run

post.summary: Cancel a queued or running agent run
post.description: The run becomes `cancelled` at once (its streaming message too) and its `chat.turn` job is cancelled (the worker gets `job.cancel`). Further worker writes are refused. Cancelling a cancelled run is a no-op; a completed or failed run gives 409.

get.summary: List content plans (newest first)
Get a plan with its items

patch.summary: Edit a draft or proposed plan
patch.description: `revision` must equal the plan's current revision (409 otherwise). `items` replaces the list: entries with `id` keep and update that item, entries without `id` are new, missing items are removed. The revision goes up by one.

post.summary: Accept a proposed plan (creates draft content items)
post.description: Requires the revision the user reviewed. Every item not in `skipItemIds` gets a draft content item (type, title, brief and platforms from the item; no generation yet) and becomes `accepted`; skipped items become `skipped`.

post.summary: Reject a draft or proposed plan
Request generation for accepted plan items
post.description: Creates one `content.generate` job per item (payload: `ContentGeneratePayload`). Without `itemIds`: only the items that still need a design (no successful generation yet, or the last one failed or was stopped), never a post that is generating, in the trash, edited or uploaded, approved, scheduled or published, nor an item the user makes by hand (`generate: false`) — those come back in `skipped`. Named items must be accepted, still have their post and not be generating; one that already has a design or is made by hand needs `force`, an edited or approved one also `overwriteEdits` (the user confirmed); published posts are never regenerated (409 with one issue per item).

post.summary: Add an item to a plan (at the end)
post.description: Draft / proposed plans: a plan edit (revision + 1). Accepted plans: the item is accepted at once and gets a draft post (no generation yet). The date must be inside the plan period. Rejected / superseded plans: 409.

200.description: The plan with the new item.

patch.description: Draft / proposed plans: a plan edit (revision + 1). Accepted plans: the item's draft post follows (title, brief, platforms; the type only while the post has no design, platforms not once it is approved or scheduled — 409). Dates stay inside the period.

delete.description: Draft / proposed plans keep at least one item (400). In an accepted plan the item's post goes to the trash when it has no design and nothing is running for it (`trashedContentId`); a post with a design stays, only the plan forgets it.

get.summary: The brand's special-day settings
get.description: Sector tags and switched-off categories; defaults (`updatedAt: null`) with tags suggested from the profile and products until saved once.

get.summary: What the plan agent reads before planning a period
get.description: The period's special days for this brand, its settings, and its history from the first day of the month three months before the period to the period's end.

get.summary: Special days between two dates
get.description: Türkiye's public holidays, religious, remembrance, commercial and social days; with `brandId` the brand's sector days and settings apply (otherwise no sector days).

get.summary: Bayram date corrections
get.description: Per year, the first day of Ramazan / Kurban Bayramı where it differs.

post.summary: Start (or restart) a run and get the turn context
post.description: `attempt` is the attempt number from `job.dispatch`. Queued -> running. Repeating it with the same attempt only returns the context. A higher attempt (the job was retried) clears the assistant message written by the previous attempt.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

get.summary: Read the turn context again (no state change)
get.description: Use it to pick up a question's answer while the run waits for it.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

get.summary: Read the run and its assistant message (no state change)
get.description: Cheaper than `context`: what the worker polls while a question or a consent card waits for the owner. `message` is null before the first write.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: Write to the run's assistant message (text deltas, parts)
post.description: Ops apply in order, all or nothing. The assistant message is created by the first write. `text.delta` appends to a text part (seq per part from 1; an applied seq is skipped, a gap is 409). `part.set` appends at the next index or replaces a part of the same type. Deltas are at most 16 KiB, a text part 100 KB, a message 512 KB (413 beyond).

200.description: The run and the message after the ops.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

put.summary: Create or replace the run's plan proposal
put.description: First call: a new plan (other open plans of the conversation become `superseded`) and a `plan_proposal` part on the assistant message. Later calls replace the same plan while it is draft/proposed (revision + 1); an identical body changes nothing. Sets the conversation's brand from `brandId` when it has none.

200.description: The plan and the assistant message.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: Finish the run successfully (with model / usage)

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: Finish the run with an error
post.description: The error is also appended to the assistant message as an `error` part.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

get.summary: List pending schedules (optionally due at or before `before`)
get.description: With `mode=local` schedules handed to the cloud publisher (`delivery = cloud`) are left out: the cloud publishes them, the Mac must not publish them as well.

200.description: Pending schedules ordered by scheduled time.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

get.summary: Load schedule, content, version slides and decrypted token for publishing
get.description: Only for a `pending` or `publishing` schedule (409 `invalid_transition` otherwise: a cancelled, published or failed schedule is never published) whose content approval still matches its frozen version (409 `hash_mismatch`).

200.description: Full publishing bundle with decrypted access token.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: Record publishing progress or final outcome for a schedule
post.description: Compare-and-set: `published` is final, a `cancelled` schedule takes outcomes only when its order had reached the cloud publisher (the cancel came too late there), a `failed` one takes a later `published`. Anything else is 409 `invalid_transition`.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: Record who publishes a schedule (cloud push result, or local)

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

get.summary: Cancelled schedules whose order is still at the cloud publisher
get.description: `delivery = cloud` and `cloudSyncedAt` set: the worker cancels the order there and reports `cloudSyncedAt: null`.

200.description: Schedules to cancel at the cloud.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: Take a schedule to publish it on this Mac (atomic)
post.description: A `pending` schedule moves to `publishing` (delivery `local`) only when it was not handed to the cloud publisher, its approval still matches and its time passed less than the maximum lateness ago; a later one is marked `failed` as missed instead. A local `publishing` claim older than `staleAfterMs` (its worker stopped) is taken over with the saved publisher state. Anything else is refused with a `reason` (200).

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

put.summary: Save the local publisher's state before acting on it (and refresh the claim)

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

get.summary: Local publishing claims whose worker stopped (resume them)

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

get.summary: Posts and accounts to read (with tokens), and queued comment actions
get.description: `kind=insights`: posts whose statistics are due (or every live post of a brand / post with `force`) and accounts whose follower count of today is missing. `kind=comments`: posts of the last 30 days and the queued replies / hides / deletes. Accounts paused by Meta's rate limit are left out.

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: Report statistics read (posts and accounts)

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: Report comments read (posts and accounts)

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: A comment action's progress (sending, done with the reply id, failed)

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

get.summary: What "Yanıt öner" writes from: the thread, the post, the brand's voice

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

put.summary: Store a "Yanıt öner" draft on the comment (never sent by itself)

401.description: Missing or wrong worker token (plain text).

post.summary: Create a pairing offer: code and QR secret (Mac only)
post.description: A 6-digit code valid for 120 s and a QR secret valid for 600 s; claiming with either uses up both. Invalidates the previous unused offer.

403.description: Not called from the Mac itself (`forbidden`).

post.summary: Trade a pairing code or QR secret for a device token (public)

201.description: Paired. The token is shown only here.

401.description: Wrong, expired or already used code (`unauthorized`).

get.summary: Where phones can reach this Mac
get.description: LAN addresses, Bonjour name and tunnel URL as the Mac app last published them. Paired phones refresh their saved routes with it after every connect.

put.summary: Publish where phones can reach this Mac (Mac only)
put.description: The Mac app calls this whenever its LAN addresses, the gateway port or the tunnel change. `macId` is replaced with this API's host id when it has one.

403.description: Not called from the Mac itself (`forbidden`).

get.summary: List paired devices (owner)

403.description: Not called from the Mac itself (`forbidden`).

post.summary: Revoke a paired device (owner)
post.description: Its token stops working immediately and its open live streams (jobs, conversations) are closed. Revoking twice is a no-op. A phone cannot revoke itself (409; it forgets the Mac instead).

403.description: Not called from the Mac itself (`forbidden`).
